entities.name: Amazasp II of Iberia
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Amazasp II, the last monarch of the P'arnavaziani dynasty, reigned as King (mepe) of Iberia from approximately 185 to 189 CE, according to the chronology established by Cyril Toumanoff based on medieval Georgian chronicles. His short but pivotal rule marked the end of a lineage that had governed Kartli (Iberia) for centuries, positioning him at a critical juncture in the geopolitical landscape of the South Caucasus, nestled between the encroaching influences of the Roman and Parthian Empires. His reign is significant not only for concluding a dynastic era but also for the violent circumstances of its end, which directly paved the way for the Arshakiani dynasty to ascend to the Iberian throne.

Succeeding his father, P'arsman III, Amazasp II inherited a kingdom that had long navigated the complex power dynamics between Rome and Parthia. While specific details of his internal policies are scarce in the surviving historical records, his reign is primarily characterized by its dramatic conclusion. Medieval Georgian chronicles, particularly "The Conversion of Kartli" and "The Royal Register," depict Amazasp II as a ruler whose authority was challenged by his own nobility, who sought the intervention of the Parthian Empire. This internal strife culminated in a significant military confrontation, likely near the borders of Iberia, where Amazasp II was ultimately defeated and killed in 189 CE.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Amazasp II's brief reign and violent end in 189 CE marked the definitive collapse of the centuries-old P'arnavaziani dynasty and ushered in the Arshakiani dynasty, fundamentally reorienting Iberia's political landscape and allegiances in the South Caucasus.
